name: Thermal Energy
description: Heat-gradient intelligence governing entropy flow, phase transitions, and thermodynamic equilibrium seeking across material boundaries.

core_attributes.pattern: gradient diffusion, phase transition, entropy management

scope.definition: Agreement between Carnot efficiency formula (1 - T_cold/T_hot) and measured maximum efficiency of reversible heat engines across temperature ranges from 1 K to 3000 K.

evidence.source: Carnot (1824) 'Réflexions sur la Puissance Motrice du Feu'; Callen (1985) 'Thermodynamics and an Introduction to Thermostatistics', 2nd ed., Wiley.
cross_domain_examples: Stirling engine approaching Carnot limit: measured 0.95 Carnot efficiency in optimized laboratory cycles
Peltier cooler (thermoelectric): achieves 0.30 of Carnot COP at 300 K — approaches bound at slow operation
black hole thermodynamics: Hawking-Penrose second law generalization applies Carnot bound to gravitational systems

scope.falsifiability: If any measured heat engine produces work exceeding Carnot efficiency 1-T_c/T_h across 10+ temperature cycles, the second law of thermodynamics fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Carnot efficiency is a theoretical maximum — real engines cannot achieve it due to irreversible processes (friction, finite heat transfer rates). The efficiency is only achievable in the quasi-static (infinite time) limit.
